parakeet: If we really want a fighting chance against the rising tide of religious nationalism ramping up across the globe, then we are going to have to become more strategic than reactionary. We have to learn how to use our tools appropriately. Support the hell out of our atheist call-in shows. They give skeptics everywhere a place to sharpen the tools of inquiry, critical thinking, and epistemic clarity. Volunteer with organizations that help people still navigating religious trauma. Give to the institutions willing to confront religious overreach and politics and be sure to hold them accountable for delivering more than just token victories. But beyond all of that, we need to pay attention to Christianity as it actually functions in the real world, how it operates, how it spreads, how it organizes people, how it builds loyalty, and how it accumulates power. And we need to ask, with honesty and seriousness, is this all we should be doing? Is this really all it takes? What else should we be building alongside critique? Because the moment we ask that question in good faith, we inherit a responsibility we can no longer ignore, and that's the responsibility to build. To build the kinds of social infrastructure that creates soft spaces to land and safe places to live for the people who are brave enough to make their way into a new world. Winning on all fronts will require more than being good at fighting. It will require us to become just as good at building. If they're building power through infrastructure, identity, and belonging, then our response cannot be critique alone. We have to build too. A fighting chance means more than exposing bad ideas. It means building better worlds. The future will not belong only to those who can fight well, but to those who can build what people can actually live in. What all of this should remind us is that if we want more than critique, if we want a real response to the forces shaping people's lives, we have to build something people can actually belong to. That's why Bridge City exists.
